turn.user_message: Do we need to hire anyone?
turn.context: Playbook §4, team and role changes: two separate role decisions. The busy-hours check, not the flat rule.

text: Yes. One Discharge Manager and two Discharge Executives.
The flat rule says three Executives. Your busy hours say two, one for each window.
At 40 to 45 discharges a day, the Manager is needed now. You are already there.
chat.pointer: Slide the discharges a day, and switch between the flat rule and your busy hours.
chat.invite: Next, we can see how this joins up with the bed desk.
chat.note: Size the team to your busy hours, not your daily total.
prompts: Why not one person for both jobs?
Who at the bed desk would see this?

blocks.title: One manager, two executives
blocks.deck: Two separate choices. The Manager owns the whole process. The Executives carry the work at the busy hours.

blocks.others: Everyone else records and approves a little more. That is a wider job, not a new one.

roles.name: Discharge Manager
roles.does: Owns the whole discharge process. Works with the other departments. A peer of the Bed Manager.

triggers.label: Discharges often run over the expected time

roles.name: Discharge Executives
roles.does: Own each discharge from the doctor’s first signal. Catch hold-ups as they happen.

sizing.flat_text: {n} a day at 15 each makes {k}. But the work comes in two windows, so most of the day they wait.
sizing.busy_text: Your work comes in two windows. One person anchored to each covers the peak. This is your own pattern.
sizing.recheck_text: Your busy hours were checked at 40 to 45 a day. At this number, run the check again with your times.
